APS Variable Code Atlas

Every derived variable in the APS code-sharing repository, with its output columns, coding, functions, and full source. Function names inside the code jump to their definitions, variable names jump to the variable that creates them, and every line number opens that line on GitHub.

Documents the code as of commit 6ea8edb, the latest change to APS-Code-Sharing (committed July 24, 2026). For edits or corrections, email mharhay@pennmedicine.upenn.edu
47 variable files54 output columns15 SOFA-2 fields in examples.Rmd150 R functions indexed
function() jumps to its definition sys_sepsis_0 jumps to the variable Line numbers open GitHub at that commit "View on GitHub" follows the main branch; "Permalink" stays fixed at 6ea8edb

Key assumptions and possible issues were written from reading the code, not running it. Treat them as drafts to confirm with the code authors.

Possible issues overview

These notes come from reading the code, not running it, and are drafts for discussion with the code authors. The four items below were checked directly against the source; the 103 per-variable notes have not been individually verified, and their count reflects detail, not severity.

Checked in source

Vasopressor cutoffs may be on a different scale than the dose

calc_norepi_equivalents() returns mcg/min (support_functions.R L577–612), while the cutoffs of 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 resemble mcg/kg/min values.

Affects Hypotension Severity sys, Hypotension Severity str, Septic Shock sys. Cutoff lines calc_sys_hypotension_sev_0.R L104–107, calc_str_hypotension_sev_0.R L105–111, calc_sys_septic_shock_0.R L46.

Checked in source

Original SOFA brain score adds 4 to every GCS

calc_sofa_cns() adds 4 to all GCS values, not only intubated values ending in T (support_functions.R L272). A GCS of 11 scores 0 instead of 2. The SOFA-2 version does this correctly.

Affects Organ Failure Trajectory sys.

Checked in source

Four variables share identical code

All four are 1 when organ_dysfnx_cause is code 2, so they will match for every participant.

Acute Allergic Reaction str, Acute Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia str, Diffuse Alveolar Hemorrhage str, Acute Inflammatory Drug Toxicity str.

Pattern

Missing inputs are usually coded 0, not NA

Most variables map missing or unknown inputs to 0 (absent or normal), so get_records_with_missing_values() will undercount real gaps. Type "defaults to 0" or "imputed" in the filter to list the variables involved.

Global Physiology SeveritySys6
Standard flow FiO2 is not capped at 1.0, unlike calc_pf_ratio in support_functions.R, so flows of 10 L/min or …
  • Standard flow FiO2 is not capped at 1.0, unlike calc_pf_ratio in support_functions.R, so flows of 10 L/min or more produce FiO2 of at least 0.51 and trigger A-aDO2.
  • FiO2, PaO2 and PaCO2 are looked back independently, so values from different days can be combined in one A-aDO2.
  • IMV patients with missing EPAP get no support type and no FiO2, so they are scored on PaO2 thresholds as if FiO2 were below 0.5.
  • A missing sofa_base_renal_dysnfx prevents doubling while Unknown triggers doubling, which is an inconsistent treatment of unknown baseline renal status.
  • The header says range 0 to 48 plus, but with doubled creatinine and 12 GCS points the maximum is 60.
  • MAP from the lowest SBP and lowest DBP cannot capture high MAP points accurately because the highest BP is not used.
Hypotension SeverityStr5
calc_norepi_equivalents appears to return mcg/min while the 0.1 and 0.25 cutoffs look like mcg/kg/min values; …
  • calc_norepi_equivalents appears to return mcg/min while the 0.1 and 0.25 cutoffs look like mcg/kg/min values; if so, most infusions would score 5. Worth confirming the intended units with the authors.
  • The NEE helper multiplies vasopressin units/min by 2.5 and angiotensin II by 10 while other agents stay in mcg/min, which mixes unit scales.
  • A vasopressor checked with all doses missing gets NEE 0 and is scored 3 regardless of the actual dose.
  • The none box checked with missing SBP or DBP returns NA, as does a record with no vasopressor box checked.
  • dobuta_dose and milr_dose are computed but never used.
Organ Failure TrajectorySys5
calc_sofa_cns in support_functions.R adds 4 to every GCS, so GCS 15 becomes 19 and scores NA then 0, and GCS 1…
  • calc_sofa_cns in support_functions.R adds 4 to every GCS, so GCS 15 becomes 19 and scores NA then 0, and GCS 11 scores 0, which understates CNS SOFA.
  • If the not collected fields are NA when a lab value is present, the if_else wrappers return NA and those components are always scored 0.
  • ECMO without invasive ventilation yields NA ratios and therefore 0 respiratory points.
  • Vasopressin and phenylephrine are not considered in the cardiovascular component.
  • The file name lacks the _0 suffix used by the other files, and the Day 0 function parameter name daily_dopa_dose_8a_0_mcgkg differs from the data field daily_dopa_dos_8a_0_mcgkg, though the call is positional.
PSI ScoreStr5
Missing age or missing sex makes the whole score NA because sex uses if_else without missing = 0.…
  • Missing age or missing sex makes the whole score NA because sex uses if_else without missing = 0.
  • Residence in a rehabilitation facility or LTACH is scored as nursing home residence.
  • pH and PaO2 are taken from the daily lowest value fields, and the code does not confirm the pH is arterial.
  • Baseline CNS dysfunction Yes with a chronic GCS band other than 13-14, 10-12 or 6-9, or missing, can never score altered mental status.
  • GCS values containing T are skipped and, if no other value exists, GCS defaults to 15, so intubated patients score from CAM alone.
Respiratory Failure SeveritySys5
PEEP for IMV is read from daily_epap_8a, and IMV with missing EPAP gets NA support type.…
  • PEEP for IMV is read from daily_epap_8a, and IMV with missing EPAP gets NA support type.
  • Standard flow FiO2 is not capped at 1.0, and no SpO2 above 97 exclusion is applied, unlike calc_sf_ratio in support_functions.R.
  • Missing daily SOFA data are coded as no respiratory support rather than unknown.
  • ECMO without IMV FiO2 gets type 6 but an NA S/F ratio.
  • The output columns are named resp_support_type_0 and sfratio_8a_0 rather than with the sys_ prefix.
Baseline Performance StatusSys4
Frailty value 0 means not performed yet sits on the same numeric scale as frailty codes 1 to 9, so it cannot b…
  • Frailty value 0 means not performed yet sits on the same numeric scale as frailty codes 1 to 9, so it cannot be used directly as a continuous or ordinal variable.
  • The wrapper comment says comorbidity uses Day 0 and Patient/Surrogate Interview data, but only Day 0 is used.
  • Mild liver disease requires the cirrhosis checkbox, so chronic hepatitis without the cirrhosis box checked earns no points.
  • The file name refers to performance status but the output columns are sys_frailty_status_0 and sys_comorbid_burden_0.
Gastrointestinal BleedingStr4
The header names the variable Gastrointestinal Bleeding but the code returns PRBC units from any cause, with n…
  • The header names the variable Gastrointestinal Bleeding but the code returns PRBC units from any cause, with no GI bleeding field used.
  • Imputing 1 unit when blood product status is UNK and PRBC is unchecked is a strong assumption that inflates totals.
  • Not administered with PRBC checked, or UNK with PRBC checked, matches no rule unless trx is Not Available, and produces NA.
  • Administered with PRBC checked but missing blood_prbc_units makes the whole total NA rather than falling back to another rule.
Presence of Pneumonia SyndromeSys4
The fallback rules code 0 even when daily_antibiotics_0 is Administered, so a patient with unknown opacity sta…
  • The fallback rules code 0 even when daily_antibiotics_0 is Administered, so a patient with unknown opacity status is coded 0 instead of NA.
  • The header says NA means unknown, but because the sign criterion is never NA, nearly all incomplete records are coded 0.
  • Highest temperature is not swapped with lowest temperature, although the APS file notes the high value can be lower than the low value.
  • COVID-19 code 6 and influenza codes 15 and 16 are excluded from the qualifying pathogen list.

Pipeline entry point

R/steroid-dag-variables.R sources every variable file and defines calc_all_steroid_dag_variables(), which joins every wrapper onto the distinct record_id list, and get_records_with_missing_values(), which lists the variables left NA per participant. Run it from the repository root, after sourcing support_functions.R.

Run the whole pipeline
# from the root of a local clone of APS-Code-Sharing
library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(lubridate); library(gt)
load("20260723_data.RData")   # your APS export: provides data, dictionary, codebook
source("support_functions.R")
source("R/steroid-dag-variables.R")
dag     <- calc_all_steroid_dag_variables(data, dictionary)   # one row per record_id
missing <- get_records_with_missing_values(dag)              # NA variables per record

The data file is not in the repository. examples.Rmd drops one excluded record before this call (lines 654–674).

1# ==============================================================================
2# Steroid DAG Variables
3# ==============================================================================
4#
5# This file is the starting point for deriving all steroid DAG variables for
6# APS Aim 6. Use `source("steroid-dag-variables.R")` to get access to all
7# variable functions, or source individual files for specific variables as needed.
8# In addition to source statements for each steroid DAG file, this file contains
9# two helper functions, one for calculating all DAG variables
10# (`calc_all_steroid_dag_variables()`) and one for identifying records that
11# couldn't be classified (left as NA) under one or more DAG variables
12# (`get_records_with_missing_values()`).
13#
14# A given variable may have both a "systematic" and "streamlined" version, though
15# many have only one or the other. The prefix "sys_" is used for SYSTEMATIC
16# variables and "str_" is used for STREAMLINED variables. The filename generally
17# matches the underlying function name, however, when a variable has multiple
18# component variables, the file is named more generically after the variable
19# (e.g., calc_sys_hyperglycemia_0.R).
20#
21# Each file contains a main function that contains the logic for calculating the
22# variable from the appropriate inputs and a convenience wrapper function that
23# takes the full dataset (and sometimes the data dictionary) as input, extracts
24# the necessary variables, calculates the variable (using the main function), and
25# returns a data frame with record_id and variable columns (one row per record_id).
26#
27# For example, `calc_sys_nmblockade_0.R` contains `calc_sys_nmblockade_0()` and
28# `wrapper_calc_sys_nmblockade_0()`.
29#
30# We HIGHLY recommend using the wrapper function instead of the main function,
31# because the process for extracting the necessary variables is tedious and error-prone,
32# often requiring joining multiple event labels together. The wrapper function abstracts
33# away that complexity.
34#
35# ==============================================================================

148# Helper function to identify records with missing values in any of the DAG variables
149# - Input: data frame containing all DAG variables for each record_id (output of calc_all_steroid_dag_variables)
150# - Returns: Data frame with one row for each record_id that has at least one missing value, along with the list of which variables are missing
151get_records_with_missing_values <- function(data) {
152 # For each row, find columns with NA values
153 missing_list <- lapply(1:nrow(data), function(i) {
154 row <- data[i, ]
155 missing_cols <- names(row)[sapply(row, is.na)]
156
157 if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
158 tibble(
159 record_id = data$record_id[i],
160 missing_cols = list(missing_cols)
161 )
162 } else {
163 NULL
164 }
165 })
166
167 # Combine all non-NULL results
168 bind_rows(missing_list) |>
169 arrange(record_id)
170}

SOFA-2 daily scores

The sofa scores chunk in examples.Rmd builds a long data frame data_sofa with one row per participant and study day, days -2 to 7, following Table 2 of Ranzani et al., JAMA 2025. Missing scores get a reason when the participant is out of hospital, dead, or withdrawn; otherwise the first missing day in days -2 to 0 is set to 0 and later gaps use last observation carried forward.

Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Key assumptions

Each organ score uses the single value closest to 8am, except respiratory, which uses the worst PaO2 or SpO2 of the day.

  • Standard-flow oxygen is converted to FiO2 as 0.21 plus 0.03 per L/min, capped at 1.0; room air is FiO2 0.21.
  • P/F is used when available; S/F is used only when P/F is missing, and S/F is treated as invalid when SpO2 exceeds 97%.
  • Respiratory scores of 3 or 4 require advanced support (high-flow oxygen, noninvasive or invasive ventilation, or ECMO with ventilation), or unknown support.
  • Cardiovascular scores missing infusion rates as zero, converts mcg/min to mcg/kg/min with Day 0 weight, scores ECMO as 4, and computes MAP as one third SBP plus two thirds DBP.
  • GCS values ending in T (intubated) add 4 points to the numeric score, and any delirium drug treatment would raise a brain score of 0 to 1, though the notebook does not pass that input.
  • Kidney scores 4 for chronic kidney replacement therapy or a study day between the RRT start and end dates; urine output is accepted by the function but not used.
  • Days outside hospital, after death, or after withdrawal are unmeasured, never imputed; within hospital, the first missing day in days -2 to 0 is set to 0, then last observation is carried forward.
Possible issues to confirm
  • Urine output criteria from the published SOFA-2 kidney component are not applied, which may understate oliguric kidney injury.
  • The table summary step calls tbl_summary() without loading gtsummary, so the notebook will not knit as written.

219```{r 'sofa scores', fold=TRUE}
220
221## daily in-hospital measurements needed for SOFA are all collected at the
222## 'Daily In-Hospital Forms' event. Each day has a separate set of fields,
223## e.g., daily_pa02_lowest_m2, daily_pa02_lowest_m1, daily_pa02_lowest_0, ...
224## which correspond to daily lowest PaO2 on day -2, -1, 0, ...
225
226## isolate the daily in-hospital data
227data_sofa <- data %>%
228
229 ## filter to the relevant event
230 filter(event_label == 'Daily In-Hospital Forms') %>%
231
232 ## filter out any repeat instrument rows (none of the SOFA variables are
233 ## on a repeating instrument/form)
234 filter(is.na(repeat_instrument)) %>%
235
236 ## merge data from the "Day 0" event
237 select(-m_weight_kg, -enrollment_time, -sofa_base_renal_chronic) %>%
238 left_join(data %>%
239 filter(event_label == 'Day 0') %>%
240 select(record_id, m_weight_kg, enrollment_time,
241 sofa_base_renal_chronic),
242 by='record_id') %>%
243
244 ## merge data from the "Hospital Discharge and Summary" event
245 select(-rrt_stdat, -rrt_endat) %>%
246 left_join(data %>%
247 filter(event_label == "Hospital Discharge and Summary") %>%
248 filter(is.na(repeat_instrument)) %>%
249 select(record_id, rrt_stdat, rrt_endat),
250 by='record_id') %>%
251
252 ## ensure there is exactly one row per participant; this is good practice
253 ## because some participants will not have any records for some events; this
254 ## ensures that there is a data point for each participant, even if that data
255 ## point is NA
256 right_join(data %>%
257 filter(!duplicated(record_id)) %>%
258 select(record_id),
259 by='record_id') %>%
260
261 ## select variables involved in SOFA calculations
262 select(
263 record_id,
264 m_weight_kg,
265 enrollment_time,

Active Fungal Infection

R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_active_fungal_0.R · 53 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sys_active_fungal_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_active_fungal_0(data)
Key assumptions

Active fungal infection is proxied by antifungal exposure, using medical history antifungals or Day 0 antifungal administration, not by microbiology.

  • Inputs are mhantifungals from the Day 0 event plus daily_antifungal_0 and trx_0 from the Daily In-Hospital Forms event.
  • The value 0 is assigned first when mhantifungals is No and either trx_0 is Not Available or daily_antifungal_0 is Not administered.
  • The value 1 is assigned when mhantifungals is Yes or when trx_0 is Available and daily_antifungal_0 is Administered.
  • The value 99 is assigned when mhantifungals is Unknown or daily_antifungal_0 is UNK, after the 0 and 1 rules have been checked.
  • When treatment data are Not Available the patient is assumed to have received no antifungal on Day 0.
  • Any combination not matched, such as missing mhantifungals with no Day 0 administration, returns NA.
Possible issues to confirm
  • Unknown is matched with two different labels, Unknown for mhantifungals and UNK for daily_antifungal_0, so other spellings would fall through to NA.
  • Treating trx_0 Not Available as no antifungal may misclassify patients whose Day 0 treatment data were simply not abstracted.
calc_sys_active_fungal_0()
Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Active Fungal Infection' for Day 0

Values:
- 0 = No
- 1 = Yes
- 99 = Unknown

5# Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Active Fungal Infection' for Day 0
6#
7# Values:
8# - 0 = No
9# - 1 = Yes
10# - 99 = Unknown
11calc_sys_active_fungal_0 <- function(
12 mhantifungals,
13 daily_antifungal_0,
14 trx_0
15) {
16 dplyr::case_when(
17 mhantifungals == "No" & (trx_0 == "Not Available" | daily_antifungal_0 == "Not administered") ~ 0,
18
19 mhantifungals == "Yes" | (trx_0 == "Available" & daily_antifungal_0 == "Administered") ~ 1,
20
21 is_unknown(mhantifungals) | daily_antifungal_0 == "UNK" ~ 99
22 )
23}
24
25
26# Convenience wrapper function
27# Returns a data frame with record_id and sys_active_fungal_0 columns (one row per record_id)

29 data |>
30 # Ensure one row per record_id (even if data is missing)
31 distinct(record_id) |>
32
33 left_join(
34 # Calculate sys_active_fungal_0 and join back to record_id
35 # This requires joining from multiple event labels
36 data |>
37 filter(event_label == 'Daily In-Hospital Forms') |>
38 select(record_id, daily_antifungal_0, trx_0) |>
39 left_join(
40 data |>
41 filter(event_label == 'Day 0') |>
42 select(record_id, mhantifungals),
43 by = 'record_id'
44 ) |>
45 mutate(sys_active_fungal_0 = calc_sys_active_fungal_0(
46 mhantifungals = mhantifungals,
47 daily_antifungal_0 = daily_antifungal_0,
48 trx_0 = trx_0
49 )) |>
50 select(record_id, sys_active_fungal_0),
51 by = 'record_id'
52 )
53}

Active Influenza Infection

R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_active_influenza_0.R · 59 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sys_active_influenza_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_active_influenza_0(data, dictionary)
Key assumptions

Coded 1 if any positive influenza test in the discharge summary is dated on or before enrollment, and 0 otherwise, with no unknown category.

  • Positive tests come from the Hospital Discharge and Summary event where cxpos code is 3 and resp_pathogen code is 15 or 16.
  • A test counts only if pathogen_date is less than or equal to enrollment_time from the Day 0 event, with no lower bound on test timing.
  • Patients with no qualifying test, a missing pathogen_date, or a missing enrollment_time are coded 0.
  • Records lacking a Day 0 event row return NA.
  • Only values 0 and 1 are produced, so untested patients are coded the same as negative patients.
Possible issues to confirm
  • The date comparison does not convert pathogen_date and enrollment_time to a common class, so a date versus datetime mismatch could give invalid results.

Values:

1## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
2## Active Influenza Infection (Systematic & Streamlined DAG)
3## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
4
5# Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Active Influenza Infection' for Day 0
6#
7# Values:
8# - 0 = No
9# - 1 = Yes
10calc_sys_active_influenza_0 <- function(has_pos_influenza_0) {
11 dplyr::case_when(
12 has_pos_influenza_0 == 1 ~ 1,
13 is.na(has_pos_influenza_0) ~ 0
14 )
15}
16
17
18# Convenience wrapper function
19# Returns a data frame with record_id and sys_active_influenza_0 columns (one row per record_id)
20wrapper_calc_sys_active_influenza_0 <- function(data, dictionary) {
21 # Get enrollment times
22 data_enrollment <- data |>
23 filter(event_label == 'Day 0') |>
24 select(record_id, enrollment_time)
25
26 # Get all positive influenza tests on or before enrollment
27 data_positive_influenza <- data |>
28 filter(event_label == 'Hospital Discharge and Summary') |>
29 left_join(
30 get_code_label_map('cxpos', dictionary),
31 by = 'cxpos'
32 ) |>
33 left_join(
34 get_code_label_map('resp_pathogen', dictionary),
35 by = 'resp_pathogen'
36 ) |>
37 filter(cxpos_code == 3 & resp_pathogen_code %in% c(15, 16)) |>
38 select(record_id, pathogen_date) |>
39 left_join(data_enrollment, by = 'record_id') |>
40 # Calculate if positive test was on or before enrollment
41 mutate(positive_before_enrollment = pathogen_date <= enrollment_time) |>
42 # Keep only tests on or before enrollment
43 filter(positive_before_enrollment) |>
44 # Group by patient and check if ANY test was positive before enrollment
45 group_by(record_id) |>
46 summarise(has_pos_influenza_0 = 1, .groups = 'drop')
47
48 # Create final classification for variable
49 data_active_influenza <- data_enrollment |>
50 left_join(data_positive_influenza, by = 'record_id') |>
51 mutate(sys_active_influenza_0 = calc_sys_active_influenza_0(
52 has_pos_influenza_0 = has_pos_influenza_0
53 )) |>
54 select(record_id, sys_active_influenza_0)
55
56 data |>
57 distinct(record_id) |>
58 left_join(data_active_influenza, by = 'record_id')
59}

Active SARS-CoV-2 Infection

R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_active_covid19_0.R · 59 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sys_active_covid19_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_active_covid19_0(data, dictionary)
Key assumptions

Coded 1 if any positive SARS-CoV-2 test in the discharge summary is dated on or before enrollment, and 0 otherwise, with no unknown category.

  • Positive tests come from the Hospital Discharge and Summary event where cxpos code is 3 and resp_pathogen code is 6.
  • A test counts only if pathogen_date is less than or equal to enrollment_time from the Day 0 event, with no lower bound on how early the test can be.
  • Any patient with no qualifying test, a missing pathogen_date, or a missing enrollment_time is coded 0, so absence of data is treated as no infection.
  • Records lacking a Day 0 event row return NA because the output is built from the Day 0 enrollment table.
  • Only values 0 and 1 are produced and there is no code for unknown or untested.
Possible issues to confirm
  • The date comparison does not convert pathogen_date and enrollment_time to a common class, so a date versus datetime mismatch could give invalid results.
  • Patients never tested are indistinguishable from patients who tested negative.

20wrapper_calc_sys_active_covid19_0 <- function(data, dictionary) {
21 # Get enrollment times
22 data_enrollment <- data |>
23 filter(event_label == 'Day 0') |>
24 select(record_id, enrollment_time)
25
26 # Get all positive COVID-19 tests on or before enrollment
27 data_positive_covid <- data |>
28 filter(event_label == 'Hospital Discharge and Summary') |>
29 left_join(
30 get_code_label_map('cxpos', dictionary),
31 by = 'cxpos'
32 ) |>
33 left_join(
34 get_code_label_map('resp_pathogen', dictionary),
35 by = 'resp_pathogen'
36 ) |>
37 filter(cxpos_code == 3 & resp_pathogen_code == 6) |>
38 select(record_id, pathogen_date) |>
39 left_join(data_enrollment, by = 'record_id') |>
40 # Calculate if positive test was on or before enrollment
41 mutate(positive_before_enrollment = pathogen_date <= enrollment_time) |>
42 # Keep only tests on or before enrollment
43 filter(positive_before_enrollment) |>
44 # Group by patient and check if ANY test was positive before enrollment
45 group_by(record_id) |>
46 summarise(has_pos_covid_0 = 1, .groups = 'drop')
47
48 # Create final classification for variable
49 data_active_covid19 <- data_enrollment |>
50 left_join(data_positive_covid, by = 'record_id') |>
51 mutate(sys_active_covid19_0 = calc_sys_active_covid19_0(
52 has_pos_covid_0 = has_pos_covid_0
53 )) |>
54 select(record_id, sys_active_covid19_0)
55
56 data |>
57 distinct(record_id) |>
58 left_join(data_active_covid19, by = 'record_id')
59}

Baseline Performance Status

R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_baseline_performance_status_0.R · 285 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sys_frailty_status_0sys_comorbid_burden_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_baseline_performance_status_0(data, dictionary)
Key assumptions

Returns two variables, Clinical Frailty Scale code with 0 for not performed, and a Charlson Comorbidity Index where unknown severity is scored as the milder category.

  • Frailty comes from the Patient/Surrogate Interview event, returning 0 when frailty_perf is No, the numeric frailty_base code when Yes, and 99 when Yes but frailty_base is missing.
  • Charlson inputs come only from the Day 0 event checkboxes and severity fields, with no age points.
  • Unknown cirrhosis severity counts as mild liver disease, unknown diabetes severity as uncomplicated, and unknown metastasis status as tumor without metastasis.
  • Chronic pulmonary disease includes asthma, interstitial lung disease, COPD and obstructive sleep apnea, each contributing a single shared point.
  • Renal disease earns 2 points only for baseline creatinine above 3.0 mg/dL or chronic kidney replacement therapy, and AIDS uses m_immunosup_conditions___5 for 6 points.
  • Checkboxes are counted without requiring the parent Yes field, and a missing value in an ungated field such as mhrheumd makes the whole score NA.
Possible issues to confirm
  • Frailty value 0 means not performed yet sits on the same numeric scale as frailty codes 1 to 9, so it cannot be used directly as a continuous or ordinal variable.
  • The wrapper comment says comorbidity uses Day 0 and Patient/Surrogate Interview data, but only Day 0 is used.
  • Mild liver disease requires the cirrhosis checkbox, so chronic hepatitis without the cirrhosis box checked earns no points.
  • The file name refers to performance status but the output columns are sys_frailty_status_0 and sys_comorbid_burden_0.

5# Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Baseline Performance Status: Frailty Status'
6#
7# Values:
8# - 0 = Not performed
9# - 1 = Very Fit
10# - 2 = Fit
11# - 3 = Managing Well
12# - 4 = Living with very mild frailty
13# - 5 = Living with mild frailty
14# - 6 = Living with moderate frailty
15# - 7 = Living with severe frailty
16# - 8 = Living with very severe frailty
17# - 9 = Terminally ill
18# - 99 = Unknown
19calc_sys_frailty_status_0 <- function(
20 frailty_base_code,
21 frailty_perf
22) {
23 dplyr::case_when(
24 frailty_perf == "No" ~ 0,
25 frailty_perf == "Yes" & !is.na(frailty_base_code) ~ as.numeric(frailty_base_code),
26 frailty_perf == "Yes" & is.na(frailty_base_code) ~ 99
27 )
28}
29
30
31
32# Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Baseline Performance Status: Comorbidity Burden'
33#
34# Value: Charlson Comorbidity Index
35calc_sys_comorbid_burden_0 <- function(
36 # Cardiovascular conditions
37 m_cv_conditions___2, # CHF
38 m_cv_conditions___4, # MI
39 m_cv_conditions___6, # Peripheral vascular disease
40
41 # Neurologic conditions
42 m_neurologic_conditions___1, # Dementia
43 m_neurologic_conditions___2, # Stroke
44 m_neurologic_conditions___3, # TIA
45 m_neurologic_conditions___4, # Hemiplegia
46 m_neurologic_conditions___5, # Paraplegia
47
48 # Pulmonary conditions
49 m_pulm_conditions___1, # Asthma
50 m_pulm_conditions___2, # Interstitial lung disease
51 m_pulm_conditions___3, # COPD
52 m_pulm_conditions___6, # Obstructive sleep apnea
53
54 # Kidney and liver conditions
55 m_kid_liver_conditions___1, # Chronic kidney disease
56 m_kid_liver_conditions___2, # Cirrhosis
57 mhckdsev, # CKD severity
58 mhhepsev, # Liver disease severity
59 mhhepfail, # Hepatic failure
60
61 # Endocrine conditions
62 m_endo_conditions___1, # Diabetes
63 mhdmsev, # Diabetes severity
64
65 # Cancer conditions
66 m_cancer_conditions___1, # Leukemia
67 m_cancer_conditions___2, # Lymphoma
68 m_cancer_conditions___4, # Solid organ cancer
69 mhsolidmeta, # Solid tumor metastasis
70
71 # Immunosuppression conditions
72 m_immunosup_conditions___5, # AIDS
73
74 # Other conditions
75 mhrheumd, # Rheumatologic/connective tissue disease
76 m_eso_stom_int_conditions___1 # Peptic ulcer disease
77) {
78
79 # Initialize score at 0
80 score <- 0
81
82 # Charlson Comorbidity Index scoring (standard weights)
83
84 # 1 POINT CONDITIONS
85
86 # Myocardial infarction: +1
87 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(is_checked(m_cv_conditions___4), 1, 0)
88
89 # Congestive heart failure: +1
90 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(is_checked(m_cv_conditions___2), 1, 0)
91
92 # Peripheral vascular disease: +1
93 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(is_checked(m_cv_conditions___6), 1, 0)
94
95 # Cerebrovascular disease (stroke or TIA): +1
96 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(
97 is_checked(m_neurologic_conditions___2) | is_checked(m_neurologic_conditions___3),
98 1,
99 0
100 )
101
102 # Dementia: +1
103 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(is_checked(m_neurologic_conditions___1), 1, 0)
104
105 # Chronic pulmonary disease: +1
106 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(
107 is_checked(m_pulm_conditions___1) |
108 is_checked(m_pulm_conditions___2) |
109 is_checked(m_pulm_conditions___3) |
110 is_checked(m_pulm_conditions___6),
111 1,
112 0
113 )
114
115 # Connective tissue disease: +1
116 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(mhrheumd == "Yes", 1, 0)
117
118 # Ulcer disease: +1
119 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(is_checked(m_eso_stom_int_conditions___1), 1, 0)
120
121 # Mild liver disease: +1
122 # (has liver disease AND (mild severity OR unknown severity) AND (no hepatic failure OR unknown failure))
123 # Note: Only count if NOT moderate/severe (checked later)
124 has_mild_liver <- is_checked(m_kid_liver_conditions___2) &
125 (mhhepsev == "Mild (chronic hepatitis w/o portal HTN)" |
126 mhhepsev == "Unknown cirrhosis severity") &
127 (mhhepfail == "No" | mhhepfail == "Unknown")
128 mild_liver_points <- dplyr::if_else(has_mild_liver, 1, 0)
129
130 # Diabetes uncomplicated: +1
131 # (has diabetes AND (mild/uncomplicated severity OR unknown severity))
132 # Note: Only count if NOT complicated (checked later)
133 has_diabetes_uncomplicated <- is_checked(m_endo_conditions___1) &
134 (mhdmsev == "Uncomplicated: treated with insulin or oral diabetic medication, no end organ damage" |
135 mhdmsev == "Unknown severity")
136 diabetes_uncomplicated_points <- dplyr::if_else(has_diabetes_uncomplicated, 1, 0)
137
138 # 2 POINT CONDITIONS
139
140 # Hemiplegia or paraplegia: +2
141 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(
142 is_checked(m_neurologic_conditions___4) | is_checked(m_neurologic_conditions___5),
143 2,
144 0
145 )
146
147 # Moderate or severe renal disease: +2
148 # (has CKD AND severity is moderate (2) OR severe (3))
149 has_mod_severe_renal <- is_checked(m_kid_liver_conditions___1) &
150 (mhckdsev == "Baseline (before acute illness) creatinine >3.0 mg/dl" |
151 mhckdsev == "Chronic kidney replacement therapy (such as hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis)")
152 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(has_mod_severe_renal, 2, 0)
153
154 # Diabetes with end organ damage: +2
155 # (has diabetes AND complicated/severe)
156 has_diabetes_complicated <- is_checked(m_endo_conditions___1) &
157 (mhdmsev == "Complicated: treated with insulin or oral diabetic medication, end-organ damage present")
158 diabetes_complicated_points <- dplyr::if_else(has_diabetes_complicated, 2, 0)
159
160 # Add diabetes points (only one or the other, not both, preference to complicated if both checked)
161 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(
162 has_diabetes_complicated,
163 diabetes_complicated_points,
164 diabetes_uncomplicated_points
165 )
166
167 # Any tumor without metastasis: +2
168 # (has solid tumor AND (no mets OR unknown mets))
169 # Note: Only count if NOT metastatic (checked later)
170 has_tumor_no_mets <- is_checked(m_cancer_conditions___4) &
171 (mhsolidmeta == "No" | mhsolidmeta == "Unknown")
172 tumor_no_mets_points <- dplyr::if_else(has_tumor_no_mets, 2, 0)
173
174 # Leukemia: +2
175 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(is_checked(m_cancer_conditions___1), 2, 0)
176
177 # Lymphoma: +2
178 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(is_checked(m_cancer_conditions___2), 2, 0)
179
180 # 3 POINT CONDITIONS
181
182 # Moderate or severe liver disease: +3
183 # (has liver disease AND (moderate severity (2) OR severe severity (3) OR hepatic failure))
184 # Note: Only count if NOT mild (replaces mild liver score)
185 has_mod_severe_liver <- is_checked(m_kid_liver_conditions___2) &
186 (mhhepsev == "Mod (cirrhosis with portal HTN)" |
187 mhhepsev == "Severe (cirrhosis with portal HTN & variceal bleed)" |
188 mhhepfail == "Yes")
189 mod_severe_liver_points <- dplyr::if_else(has_mod_severe_liver, 3, 0)
190
191 # Add liver points (only one or the other, not both)
192 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(
193 has_mod_severe_liver,
194 mod_severe_liver_points,
195 mild_liver_points
196 )
197
198 # 6 POINT CONDITIONS
199
200 # Metastatic solid tumor: +6
201 # (has solid tumor AND has metastasis)
202 # Note: Only count if metastatic (replaces non-metastatic score)
203 has_tumor_with_mets <- is_checked(m_cancer_conditions___4) & mhsolidmeta == "Yes"
204 tumor_with_mets_points <- dplyr::if_else(has_tumor_with_mets, 6, 0)
205
206 # Add solid tumor points (only one or the other, not both)
207 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(
208 has_tumor_with_mets,
209 tumor_with_mets_points,
210 tumor_no_mets_points
211 )
212
213 # AIDS: +6
214 score <- score + dplyr::if_else(is_checked(m_immunosup_conditions___5), 6, 0)
215
216 return(score)
217}
218

Chronic Immunocompromise

R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_chron_immunocomp_0.R · 68 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sys_chron_immunocomp_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_chron_immunocomp_0(data)
Key assumptions

Coded 1 when m_immunosuppression is Yes and any of immunosuppression conditions 2 to 7 or 88 is checked, with condition 1 deliberately excluded.

  • All inputs come from the Day 0 event.
  • The value 0 requires m_immunosuppression to be Yes or No and all of conditions 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 88 to be unchecked.
  • Condition 1 is not considered, so a patient whose only immunosuppression is condition 1 is coded 0.
  • The value 99 is assigned when m_immunosuppression is Unknown.
  • A missing m_immunosuppression, or No with a condition box checked, returns NA.
Possible issues to confirm
  • Inconsistent entries where m_immunosuppression is No but a condition is checked fall through to NA without a flag.

Chronic Moderate-Dose Steroid Use

Compare with the streamlined version
R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_chron_steroid_moddose_0.R · 53 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sys_chron_steroid_moddose_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_chron_steroid_moddose_0(data)
Key assumptions

Chronic moderate-dose steroid use relies on mhccster Yes, but any documented adrenal insufficiency forces the value to 0 even when steroids are reported.

  • All inputs come from the Day 0 event, and the dose threshold is not coded but inherited from the mhccster field definition.
  • The value 0 is assigned first if mhccster is No, or endocrine condition 2 is checked under m_endocrine Yes, or immunosuppression condition 1 is checked under m_immunosuppression Yes.
  • The value 1 requires mhccster Yes with both parent fields answered Yes or No and both adrenal indicators unchecked.
  • The value 99 is assigned when any of mhccster, m_endocrine or m_immunosuppression is Unknown, but only after the 0 rule, so mhccster No overrides an unknown parent.
  • Missing parent fields with mhccster Yes return NA.
Possible issues to confirm
  • Patients on chronic steroids who also have the adrenal insufficiency indicators are coded 0, which an analyst may not expect from the variable name.

17) {
18 dplyr::case_when(
19 mhccster == "No" |

26
27 is_unknown(mhccster) | is_unknown(m_endocrine) | is_unknown(m_immunosuppression) ~ 99
28 )

wrapper_calc_sys_def_adrenal_insufficiency_0(data)
Key assumptions

Definite adrenal insufficiency is coded 1 from history checkboxes only, endocrine condition 2 or immunosuppression condition 1, with no laboratory criteria.

  • All inputs come from the Day 0 event.
  • The value 0 requires both m_endocrine and m_immunosuppression answered Yes or No and both endocrine condition 2 and immunosuppression condition 1 unchecked.
  • The value 1 is assigned when either indicator is checked with its parent field equal to Yes.
  • The value 99 is assigned when either parent field is Unknown and no indicator is positive.
  • Missing parent fields, or a checked box under a parent of No, return NA.

11calc_sys_def_adrenal_insufficiency_0 <- function(
12 m_endocrine,

Delirium

R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_delirium_0.R · 111 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sys_delirium_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_delirium_0(data)
Key assumptions

Uses CAM over Day -2 to Day 0, coding 0 only if all three days are negative, 1 if any day is positive, and 2 otherwise.

  • Inputs are cam, lowrass_orres and highestrass_orres for Days 0, -1 and -2 from the Daily In-Hospital Forms event.
  • Rule order is all negative, then any positive, then any Not done, then CAM missing for a branching reason.
  • A positive CAM on any single day yields 1 even if other days are missing.
  • CAM is treated as correctly missing when either RASS is missing or both RASS values are -4 or -5, and that case is coded 2.
  • Value 2 therefore combines CAM not done, deep sedation or coma, and missing RASS.
  • A missing CAM despite valid RASS with no other qualifying day returns NA.
Possible issues to confirm
  • A patient negative on Days 0 and -1 but with no CAM on Day -2 because of branching logic is coded 2 rather than 0.
  • The header describes 2 as CAM not done, but it also captures RASS -4 or -5 and missing RASS.
  • RASS values are compared numerically to -4 and -5, which would fail silently if the export stores RASS as text labels.
calc_sys_delirium_0()
Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Delirium'

Values:
- 0 = CAM done and delirium not present
- 1 = CAM done and delirium present
- 2 = CAM not done

1## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
2## Delirium (Systematic & Streamlined DAG)
3## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
4
5# Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Delirium'
6#
7# Values:
8# - 0 = CAM done and delirium not present
9# - 1 = CAM done and delirium present
10# - 2 = CAM not done
11calc_sys_delirium_0 <- function(
12 # Core inputs
13 cam_0,
14 cam_m1,
15 cam_m2,
16 # Branching logic
17 lowrass_orres_0,
18 lowrass_orres_m1,
19 lowrass_orres_m2,
20 highestrass_orres_0,
21 highestrass_orres_m1,
22 highestrass_orres_m2
23 ) {
24
25 positive_text <- "Positive for delirium at least once on this day"
26 negative_text <- "Negative for delirium on all assessments on this day"
27 not_done_text <- "Not done"
28
29 ## Check if all CAM assessments are negative
30 all_negative <- (
31 cam_m2 == negative_text &
32 cam_m1 == negative_text &
33 cam_0 == negative_text
34 )
35
36 ## Check if any CAM assessment is positive
37 any_positive <- (
38 cam_m2 == positive_text |
39 cam_m1 == positive_text |
40 cam_0 == positive_text
41 )
42
43 ## Check if any CAM assessment was "Not done"
44 any_not_done <- (
45 cam_m2 == "Not done" |
46 cam_m1 == "Not done" |
47 cam_0 == "Not done"
48 )
49
50 ## Check branching logic: cam should be visible if RASS scores are available and not both -4/-5
51 ## For each day, check if cam is missing because branching logic was NOT satisfied (correctly hidden)
52
53 # cam_0 branching logic: visible if both RASS scores exist and at least one is not -4 or -5
54 cam_0_should_be_visible <- (!is.na(lowrass_orres_0) & !is.na(highestrass_orres_0)) &
55 ((lowrass_orres_0 != -4 & lowrass_orres_0 != -5) |
56 (highestrass_orres_0 != -4 & highestrass_orres_0 != -5))
57 cam_0_correctly_missing <- is.na(cam_0) & !cam_0_should_be_visible
58
59 # cam_m1 branching logic: visible if both RASS scores exist and at least one is not -4 or -5
60 cam_m1_should_be_visible <- (!is.na(lowrass_orres_m1) & !is.na(highestrass_orres_m1)) &
61 ((lowrass_orres_m1 != -4 & lowrass_orres_m1 != -5) |
62 (highestrass_orres_m1 != -4 & highestrass_orres_m1 != -5))
63 cam_m1_correctly_missing <- is.na(cam_m1) & !cam_m1_should_be_visible
64
65 # cam_m2 branching logic: visible if both RASS scores exist and at least one is not -4 or -5
66 cam_m2_should_be_visible <- (!is.na(lowrass_orres_m2) & !is.na(highestrass_orres_m2)) &
67 ((lowrass_orres_m2 != -4 & lowrass_orres_m2 != -5) |
68 (highestrass_orres_m2 != -4 & highestrass_orres_m2 != -5))
69 cam_m2_correctly_missing <- is.na(cam_m2) & !cam_m2_should_be_visible
70
71 ## Check if any cam is correctly missing due to branching logic not being satisfied
72 any_correctly_missing_due_to_branching <- cam_0_correctly_missing |
73 cam_m1_correctly_missing |
74 cam_m2_correctly_missing
75
76 ## Return result
77 dplyr::case_when(
78 all_negative ~ 0, # All negative
79 any_positive ~ 1, # Delirium present (at least one positive)
80 any_not_done ~ 2, # At least one "Not done"
81 any_correctly_missing_due_to_branching ~ 2 # CAM correctly missing due to branching logic
82 )
83}
84
85
86# Convenience wrapper function
87# Returns a data frame with record_id and sys_delirium_0 columns (one row per record_id)
88wrapper_calc_sys_delirium_0 <- function(data) {
89 data_with_delirium <- data |>
90 filter(event_label == 'Daily In-Hospital Forms') |>
91 mutate(
92 sys_delirium_0 = calc_sys_delirium_0(
93 cam_0 = cam_0,
94 cam_m1 = cam_m1,
95 cam_m2 = cam_m2,
96
97 lowrass_orres_0 = lowrass_orres_0,
98 lowrass_orres_m1 = lowrass_orres_m1,
99 lowrass_orres_m2 = lowrass_orres_m2,
100
101 highestrass_orres_0 = highestrass_orres_0,
102 highestrass_orres_m1 = highestrass_orres_m1,
103 highestrass_orres_m2 = highestrass_orres_m2
104 )
105 ) |>
106 select(record_id, sys_delirium_0)
107
108 data |>
109 distinct(record_id) |>
110 left_join(data_with_delirium, by = 'record_id')
111}

Global Physiology Severity

R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_global_phys_sev_0.R · 802 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sys_global_phys_sev_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_global_phys_sev_0(data, dictionary)
Key assumptions

APACHE II Acute Physiology Score where every missing component, and FiO2 or GCS that cannot be determined, is imputed as normal with 0 points.

  • Vital signs come from the Day 0 event only, while labs, blood gases and GCS use Day 0 with lookback to Day -1 then Day -2 from the Daily In-Hospital Forms event.
  • Temperature, heart rate and respiratory rate use the more extreme of the high and low values, and MAP is computed from the lowest SBP and lowest DBP.
  • Oxygenation scores 4 for ECMO codes 1 or 2, uses A-aDO2 when FiO2 is at least 0.5 with PaCO2 and PaO2 available, and otherwise uses PaO2 thresholds 70, 61 and 55.
  • FiO2 is derived from calc_resp_support_type in calc_sys_resp_failure_sev_0.R, with standard flow as 0.21 plus 0.03 times litres per minute, and missing FiO2 is treated as below 0.5.
  • Creatinine points are doubled to 4, 6 or 8 unless sofa_base_renal_dysnfx is Yes with a baseline category that rules out doubling, so absence of baseline dysfunction is treated as acute renal failure.
  • GCS uses the most recent non-intubated value over three days and defaults to 15, which is 0 points, when only T values or not documented are present.
  • The total coalesces every NA component to 0, so the score is never NA for a patient with a Day 0 row.
Possible issues to confirm
  • Standard flow FiO2 is not capped at 1.0, unlike calc_pf_ratio in support_functions.R, so flows of 10 L/min or more produce FiO2 of at least 0.51 and trigger A-aDO2.
  • FiO2, PaO2 and PaCO2 are looked back independently, so values from different days can be combined in one A-aDO2.
  • IMV patients with missing EPAP get no support type and no FiO2, so they are scored on PaO2 thresholds as if FiO2 were below 0.5.
  • A missing sofa_base_renal_dysnfx prevents doubling while Unknown triggers doubling, which is an inconsistent treatment of unknown baseline renal status.
  • The header says range 0 to 48 plus, but with doubled creatinine and 12 GCS points the maximum is 60.
  • MAP from the lowest SBP and lowest DBP cannot capture high MAP points accurately because the highest BP is not used.

1## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
2## 1. APS Temperature Score
3## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
4
5# Calculates APS temperature score component
6calc_aps_temp_score <- function(
7 hightemp_vsorres,
8 lowtemp_vsorres
9) {
10 # 1. Temperature (rectal, °C) - use most extreme
11 # - Get highest and lowest temp (`hightemp_vsorres` can be lower than `lowtemp_vsorres`)
12 temp_high <- pmax(hightemp_vsorres, lowtemp_vsorres)
13 temp_low <- pmin(hightemp_vsorres, lowtemp_vsorres)
14
15 # - Calculate APS temperature points
16 temp_points <- dplyr::case_when(
17 temp_high >= 41 | temp_low < 30 ~ 4,
18 temp_high >= 39 | temp_low < 32 ~ 3,
19 temp_low < 34 ~ 2,
20 temp_high >= 38.5 | temp_low < 36 ~ 1,
21 temp_high >= 36 | temp_low < 38.5 ~ 0
22 )
23
24 return(temp_points)
25}
26
27## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
28## 2. APS Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) Score
29## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
30
31# Calculates APS MAP score component
32calc_aps_map_score <- function(
33 lowsysbp_vsorres,
34 lowdbp_vsorres
35) {
36 # 2. Mean Arterial Pressure (mmHg)
37 # - Calculate MAP from systolic and diastolic BP
38 map <- (lowsysbp_vsorres + (2 * lowdbp_vsorres)) / 3
39
40 # - Calculate APS MAP points
41 map_points <- dplyr::case_when(
42 map >= 160 ~ 4,
43 map >= 130 ~ 3,
44 map >= 110 ~ 2,
45 map >= 70 ~ 0,
46 map >= 50 ~ 2,
47 map < 50 ~ 4
48 )
49
50 return(map_points)
51}
52

54## 3. APS Heart Rate Score
55## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
56
57# Calculates APS heart rate score component
58calc_aps_hr_score <- function(
59 highhr_vsorres,
60 lowhr_vsorres
61) {
62 # 3. Heart Rate (bpm) - use most extreme
63 # - Get highest and lowest heart rate (`highhr_vsorres` can be lower than `lowhr_vsorres`)
64 hr_high <- pmax(highhr_vsorres, lowhr_vsorres)
65 hr_low <- pmin(highhr_vsorres, lowhr_vsorres)
66
67 # - Calculate APS heart rate points
68 hr_points <- dplyr::case_when(
69 hr_high >= 180 | hr_low < 40 ~ 4,
70 hr_high >= 140 | hr_low < 55 ~ 3,
71 hr_high >= 110 | hr_low < 70 ~ 2,
72 hr_high >= 70 | hr_low < 110 ~ 0
73 )
74
75 return(hr_points)
76}

82# Calculates APS respiratory rate score component
83calc_aps_rr_score <- function(
84 highrr_vsorres,
85 lowrr_vsorres
86) {
87 # 4. Respiratory Rate (breaths/min) - use worst (most extreme)
88 # - Get highest and lowest respiratory rate (`highrr_vsorres` can be lower than `lowrr_vsorres`)
89 rr_high <- pmax(highrr_vsorres, lowrr_vsorres)
90 rr_low <- pmin(highrr_vsorres, lowrr_vsorres)
91
92 # - Calculate APS respiratory rate points
93 rr_points <- dplyr::case_when(
94 rr_high >= 50 | rr_low < 6 ~ 4,
95 rr_high >= 35 ~ 3,
96 rr_low < 10 ~ 2,
97 rr_high >= 25 | rr_low < 12 ~ 1,
98 rr_high >= 12 | rr_low < 25 ~ 0,
99 )
100
101 return(rr_points)
102}

105## 5. APS Oxygenation Score
106## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
107
108# Calculates APS oxygenation score component
109# Uses A-aDO2 if FiO2 >= 0.5, else uses PaO2
110calc_aps_oxy_score <- function(
111 resp_support_type_0, # Calculated by calc_resp_support_type()
112 resp_support_type_m1, # Calculated by calc_resp_support_type()
113 resp_support_type_m2, # Calculated by calc_resp_support_type()
114
115 daily_resp_8a_0_code,
116 daily_resp_8a_m1_code,
117 daily_resp_8a_m2_code,
118
119 daily_standard_flow_8a_0,
120 daily_standard_flow_8a_m1,
121 daily_standard_flow_8a_m2,
122
123 daily_hfnc_fi02_8a_0,
124 daily_hfnc_fi02_8a_m1,
125 daily_hfnc_fi02_8a_m2,
126
127 daily_niv_fi02_8a_0,
128 daily_niv_fi02_8a_m1,
129 daily_niv_fi02_8a_m2,
130
131 daily_imv_fio2_8a_0,
132 daily_imv_fio2_8a_m1,
133 daily_imv_fio2_8a_m2,
134
135 daily_pa02_lowest_0,
136 daily_pa02_lowest_m1,
137 daily_pa02_lowest_m2,
138
139 daily_paco2_lowest_0,
140 daily_paco2_lowest_m1,
141 daily_paco2_lowest_m2
142) {
143 # 5. Oxygenation: A-aDO2 if FiO2 >= 0.5, else PaO2
144
145 # Determine FiO2 based on respiratory support type (using helper function)
146 # - If FiO2 is still missing after this, it will be treated as < 0.5 for APS calculation purposes
147
148 ## Get FiO2 for each day
149 fio2_0 <- calc_fio2_from_resp_support(
150 resp_support_type_0,
151 daily_standard_flow_8a_0,
152 daily_hfnc_fi02_8a_0,
153 daily_niv_fi02_8a_0,
154 daily_imv_fio2_8a_0
155 )
156
157 fio2_m1 <- calc_fio2_from_resp_support(
158 resp_support_type_m1,
159 daily_standard_flow_8a_m1,
160 daily_hfnc_fi02_8a_m1,
161 daily_niv_fi02_8a_m1,
162 daily_imv_fio2_8a_m1
163 )
164
165 fio2_m2 <- calc_fio2_from_resp_support(
166 resp_support_type_m2,
167 daily_standard_flow_8a_m2,
168 daily_hfnc_fi02_8a_m2,
169 daily_niv_fi02_8a_m2,
170 daily_imv_fio2_8a_m2
171 )
172
173 ## Get final FiO2 with lookback (Day 0 -> Day -1 -> Day -2)
174 fio2 <- get_value_with_lookback(fio2_0, fio2_m1, fio2_m2)
175
176 # Track which day FiO2 came from (0 = Day 0, 1 = Day -1, 2 = Day -2)
177 fio2_day <- dplyr::case_when(
178 !is.na(fio2_0) ~ 0,
179 !is.na(fio2_m1) ~ 1,
180 !is.na(fio2_m2) ~ 2
181 )
182
183 # Check if patient is on ECMO, but only if ECMO occurred on same or earlier day than FiO2
184 resp_code <- get_value_with_lookback(daily_resp_8a_0_code, daily_resp_8a_m1_code, daily_resp_8a_m2_code)
185
186 # Track which day resp_code came from (0 = Day 0, 1 = Day -1, 2 = Day -2)
187 resp_code_day <- dplyr::case_when(
188 !is.na(daily_resp_8a_0_code) ~ 0,
189 !is.na(daily_resp_8a_m1_code) ~ 1,
190 !is.na(daily_resp_8a_m2_code) ~ 2
191 )
192
193 # ECMO is only prioritized if it occurred on an earlier or same available day as FiO2
194 is_ecmo <- !is.na(resp_code) & resp_code %in% c(1, 2) &
195 (is.na(fio2_day) | (resp_code_day <= fio2_day))
196
197 # Get PaO2 and PaCO2 with lookback
198 pao2 <- get_value_with_lookback(daily_pa02_lowest_0, daily_pa02_lowest_m1, daily_pa02_lowest_m2)
199 paco2 <- get_value_with_lookback(daily_paco2_lowest_0, daily_paco2_lowest_m1, daily_paco2_lowest_m2)
200
201 # Calculate A-aDO2 if FiO2 >= 0.5
202 # A-aDO2 = (FiO2 * (760 - 47)) - (PaCO2 / 0.8) - PaO2
203 aado2 <- ifelse(!is.na(fio2) & fio2 >= 0.5 & !is.na(paco2) & !is.na(pao2),
204 (fio2 * (760 - 47)) - (paco2 / 0.8) - pao2,
205 NA)
206
207 oxy_points <- dplyr::case_when(
208 # ECMO patients (daily_resp_8a_0_code %in% c(1, 2)) get maximum severity (4 points)
209 is_ecmo ~ 4,
210 # A-aDO2 used if FiO2 >= 0.5
211 !is.na(aado2) & aado2 >= 500 ~ 4,
212 !is.na(aado2) & aado2 >= 350 ~ 3,
213 !is.na(aado2) & aado2 >= 200 ~ 2,
214 !is.na(aado2) & aado2 < 200 ~ 0,
215 # PaO2 used if FiO2 < 0.5 or A-aDO2 not calculable
216 !is.na(pao2) & pao2 > 70 ~ 0,
217 !is.na(pao2) & pao2 >= 61 ~ 1,
218 !is.na(pao2) & pao2 >= 55 ~ 3,
219 !is.na(pao2) & pao2 < 55 ~ 4,
220 # Impute normal (0 points) if measurement is missing
221 .default = 0
222 )
223
224 return(oxy_points)
225}

286# Calculates APS serum potassium score component
287calc_aps_potassium_score <- function(
288 daily_k_8a_0,
289 daily_k_8a_m1,
290 daily_k_8a_m2
291) {
292 # 8. Serum Potassium (mmol/L)
293 potassium <- get_value_with_lookback(daily_k_8a_0, daily_k_8a_m1, daily_k_8a_m2)
294
295 k_points <- dplyr::case_when(
296 potassium >= 7 ~ 4,
297 potassium >= 6 ~ 3,
298 potassium >= 5.5 ~ 1,
299 potassium >= 3.5 ~ 0,
300 potassium >= 3 ~ 1,
301 potassium >= 2.5 ~ 2,
302 potassium < 2.5 ~ 4
303 )
304
305 return(k_points)
306}

308## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
309## 9. APS Serum Creatinine Score
310## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
311
312# Calculates APS serum creatinine score component
313# Note: Points can be doubled for acute renal failure
314calc_aps_creatinine_score <- function(
315 daily_cr_8a_0,
316 daily_cr_8a_m1,
317 daily_cr_8a_m2,
318 sofa_base_renal_dysnfx,
319 sofa_base_renal_chronic
320) {
321 # 9. Serum Creatinine (mg/dL)
322 creatinine <- get_value_with_lookback(daily_cr_8a_0, daily_cr_8a_m1, daily_cr_8a_m2)
323
324 cr_points <- dplyr::case_when(
325
326 # Check whether or not to double points
327 creatinine >= 3.5 & (
328 sofa_base_renal_dysnfx != "Yes" |
329 (
330 sofa_base_renal_dysnfx == "Yes" &
331 sofa_base_renal_chronic %in% c(
332 "Creatinine 1.2 - 1.9 mg/dL",
333 "Creatinine 2.0 - 3.4 mg/dL"
334 )
335 )
336 ) ~ 8,
337 creatinine >= 3.5 ~ 4,
338
339 # Check whether or not to double points
340 creatinine >= 2 & (
341 sofa_base_renal_dysnfx != "Yes" |
342 (sofa_base_renal_dysnfx == "Yes" & sofa_base_renal_chronic == "Creatinine 1.2 - 1.9 mg/dL")
343 ) ~ 6,
344 creatinine >= 2 ~ 3,
345
346 # # Check whether or not to double points
347 creatinine >= 1.5 & sofa_base_renal_dysnfx != "Yes" ~ 4,
348 creatinine >= 1.5 ~ 2,
349
350 # Don't double these two
351 creatinine >= 0.6 ~ 0,
352 creatinine < 0.6 ~ 2
353 )
354
355 return(cr_points)
356}
357

359## 10. APS Hematocrit Score
360## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
361
362# Calculates APS hematocrit score component
363calc_aps_hct_score <- function(
364 daily_hct_8a_0,
365 daily_hct_8a_m1,
366 daily_hct_8a_m2
367) {
368 # 10. Hematocrit (%)
369 hematocrit <- get_value_with_lookback(daily_hct_8a_0, daily_hct_8a_m1, daily_hct_8a_m2)
370
371 hct_points <- dplyr::case_when(
372 hematocrit >= 60 ~ 4,
373 hematocrit >= 50 ~ 2,
374 hematocrit >= 46 ~ 1,
375 hematocrit >= 30 ~ 0,
376 hematocrit >= 20 ~ 2,
377 hematocrit < 20 ~ 4
378 )
379
380 return(hct_points)
381}

384## 11. APS White Blood Cell Count Score
385## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
386
387# Calculates APS white blood cell count score component
388calc_aps_wbc_score <- function(
389 daily_wbc_8a_0,
390 daily_wbc_8a_m1,
391 daily_wbc_8a_m2
392) {
393 # 11. White Blood Cell Count (1000/mm³)
394 wbc <- get_value_with_lookback(daily_wbc_8a_0, daily_wbc_8a_m1, daily_wbc_8a_m2)
395
396 wbc_points <- dplyr::case_when(
397 wbc >= 40 ~ 4,
398 wbc >= 20 ~ 2,
399 wbc >= 15 ~ 1,
400 wbc >= 3 ~ 0,
401 wbc >= 1 ~ 2,
402 wbc < 1 ~ 4
403 )
404
405 return(wbc_points)
406}

408## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
409## 12. APS Glasgow Coma Score
410## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
411
412# Calculates APS Glasgow Coma Score component (15 - GCS)
413# - Look back to find the last available value without a T
414# - If no prior value available without a T, then assume a "normal" GCS (15)
415# This is consistent with Footnote C from the SOFA 2 paper.
416calc_aps_gcs_score <- function(
417 daily_gcs_8a_0,
418 daily_gcs_8a_m1,
419 daily_gcs_8a_m2
420) {
421
422 # Use helper function to get GCS with lookback
423 gcs <- get_gcs_with_lookback(daily_gcs_8a_0, daily_gcs_8a_m1, daily_gcs_8a_m2)
424
425 # Extract quantitative component of GCS
426 gcs <- as.numeric(gcs)
427
428 # Calculate points (15 - GCS)
429 gcs_points <- 15 - gcs
430
431 return(gcs_points)
432}
433
434## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
435## APS Score (Combining All Components)
436## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
437
438# Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Global Physiology Severity'
439#
440# Value: Total APS score (sum of 12 components, range 0-48+)
441calc_sys_global_phys_sev_0 <- function(
442 aps_temp_score,
443 aps_map_score,
444 aps_hr_score,
445 aps_rr_score,
446 aps_oxy_score,
447 aps_ph_score,
448 aps_sodium_score,
449 aps_potassium_score,
450 aps_creatinine_score,
451 aps_hct_score,
452 aps_wbc_score,
453 aps_gcs_score
454) {
455 # Impute normal (0 points) for any component with NA value
456 # This allows extraction of records missing components (from earlier steps) for quality improvement
457 # while still calculating a complete APS score properly
458 total_aps <- rowSums(
459 cbind(
460 dplyr::coalesce(aps_temp_score, 0),
461 dplyr::coalesce(aps_map_score, 0),
462 dplyr::coalesce(aps_hr_score, 0),
463 dplyr::coalesce(aps_rr_score, 0),
464 dplyr::coalesce(aps_oxy_score, 0),
465 dplyr::coalesce(aps_ph_score, 0),
466 dplyr::coalesce(aps_sodium_score, 0),
467 dplyr::coalesce(aps_potassium_score, 0),
468 dplyr::coalesce(aps_creatinine_score, 0),
469 dplyr::coalesce(aps_hct_score, 0),
470 dplyr::coalesce(aps_wbc_score, 0),
471 dplyr::coalesce(aps_gcs_score, 0)
472 ),
473 na.rm = FALSE
474 )
475
476 return(total_aps)
477}

484# Helper function to calculate FiO2 from respiratory support type
485#
486# Value: FiO2 based on respiratory support type
487# - Uses the same logic as the denominator calculation in `calc_sfratio_8a_0()`
488# - to ensure consistency.
489calc_fio2_from_resp_support <- function(
490 resp_support_type, # Calculated by calc_resp_support_type()
491 standard_flow,
492 hfnc_fio2,
493 niv_fio2,
494 imv_fio2
495) {
496 dplyr::case_when(
497 resp_support_type == 1 ~ 0.21,
498 resp_support_type == 2 ~ 0.21 + (0.03 * standard_flow),
499 resp_support_type == 3 ~ hfnc_fio2,
500 resp_support_type == 4 ~ niv_fio2,
501 resp_support_type %in% c(5, 6) ~ imv_fio2
502 )
503}

Call
wrapper_calc_sys_hyperglycemia_0(data)
Key assumptions

Returns a diabetes history flag and the raw Day 0 8 am glucose in mg/dL, with -1 as a sentinel for not collected.

  • History uses m_endocrine and endocrine condition 1 from the Day 0 event, coding 0 for Yes or No with box unchecked, 1 for Yes with box checked, and 99 for Unknown.
  • History is diabetes as a comorbidity, not measured hyperglycemia.
  • Glucose uses daily_gluc_8a_0 from the Daily In-Hospital Forms event with no lookback to earlier days.
  • When glucose is missing and daily_gluc_nc_0 is Not Collected the value is -1, and otherwise a missing glucose is NA.
  • No glucose threshold is applied and the glucose value is returned unchanged.
Possible issues to confirm
  • The -1 sentinel must be recoded before glucose is modeled as continuous.
  • History entries with m_endocrine No but the diabetes box checked return NA.

5# Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Hyperglycemia: History' for Day 0
6#
7# Values:
8# - 0 = No
9# - 1 = Yes
10# - 99 = Unknown
11calc_sys_hyperglyc_hist_0 <- function(
12 m_endocrine,
13 m_endo_conditions___1
14) {
15 dplyr::case_when(
16 m_endocrine %in% c("Yes", "No") & is_unchecked(m_endo_conditions___1) ~ 0,
17 m_endocrine == "Yes" & is_checked(m_endo_conditions___1) ~ 1,
18 is_unknown(m_endocrine) ~ 99
19 )
20}
21
22
23# Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Hyperglycemia: Glucose Level' for Day 0
24#
25# Value: Glucose level in mg/dL (-1 = 'Not Collected')
26calc_sys_hyperglyc_gluc_0 <- function(
27 daily_gluc_8a_0,
28 daily_gluc_nc_0
29) {
30 dplyr::case_when(
31 !is.na(daily_gluc_8a_0) ~ daily_gluc_8a_0,
32 daily_gluc_nc_0 == 'Not Collected' ~ -1
33 )
34}

sys_hypotension_sev_0
Call

Key assumptions

Day 0 8 am ordinal hypotension score 0 to 4 built from MAP, inotropes and norepinephrine equivalents (NEE), with a 0.1 NEE cutoff between levels 3 and 4.

  • Inputs are Day 0 vasopressor checkboxes, 8 am SBP and DBP, and 8 am drug doses from the Daily In-Hospital Forms event, with weight from the Day 0 event.
  • Rule order is none box checked with MAP at least 70 gives 0, none checked with MAP below 70 gives 1, then dobutamine or milrinone only with dopamine at most 5 mcg/kg/min gives 2.
  • Next, any checked vasopressor with NEE at most 0.1 gives 3, and NEE above 0.1 gives 4 whether or not a box is checked.
  • NEE from calc_norepi_equivalents uses mcg/min doses, falling back to mcg/kg/min times weight, with factors phenylephrine divided by 10, vasopressin times 2.5, dopamine divided by 100 and angiotensin II times 10.
  • Missing doses are set to 0, so a checked vasopressor with no recorded dose scores 3.
  • Dobutamine and milrinone are excluded from NEE, and the none box checked overrides any recorded doses.
  • A none box checked with missing MAP, or all boxes unchecked with no doses, returns NA.
Possible issues to confirm
  • The NEE helper appears to return mcg/min while the 0.1 cutoff looks like a mcg/kg/min value; if so, most vasopressor doses would score 4. Worth confirming the intended units with the authors.
  • Dose fields recorded only in mcg/kg/min become 0 when weight is missing.
  • Doses of dobutamine and milrinone are computed in the function but never used.
calc_sys_hypotension_sev_0()
Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Hypotension Severity'

Values:
- 0 = No pressors or inotrope, MAP >= 70
- 1 = No pressors or inotrope, MAP < 70
- 2 = On dobutamine/milrinone only (with low/no dopamine)
- 3 = On vasopressors with NEE <= 0.1
- 4 = NEE > 0.1

5# Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Hypotension Severity'
6#
7# Values:
8# - 0 = No pressors or inotrope, MAP >= 70
9# - 1 = No pressors or inotrope, MAP < 70
10# - 2 = On dobutamine/milrinone only (with low/no dopamine)
11# - 3 = On vasopressors with NEE <= 0.1
12# - 4 = NEE > 0.1
13calc_sys_hypotension_sev_0 <- function(
14 daily_vasopressors_0___0,
15 daily_vasopressors_0___1,
16 daily_vasopressors_0___2,
17 daily_vasopressors_0___3,
18 daily_vasopressors_0___4,
19 daily_vasopressors_0___5,
20 daily_vasopressors_0___6,
21 daily_vasopressors_0___7,
22 daily_vasopressors_0___8,
23 daily_vasopressors_0___88,
24
25 daily_sbp_8a_0,
26 daily_dbp_8a_0,
27
28 daily_ne_dose_8a_0_mcg,
29 daily_ne_dose_8a_0_mcgkg,
30 daily_epi_dose_8a_0_mcg,
31 daily_epi_dose_8a_0_mcgkg,
32 daily_phen_dose_8a_0_mcg,
33 daily_phen_dos_8a_0_mcgkg,
34 daily_vaso_dose_8a_0,
35 daily_dopa_dose_8a_0_mcg,
36 daily_dopa_dos_8a_0_mcgkg,
37 daily_dobuta_8a_0_mcg,
38 daily_dobuta_8a_0_mcgkg,
39 daily_ang2_8a_0_mcg,
40 daily_ang2_8a_0_mcgkg,
41 daily_milr_8a_0_mcg,
42 daily_milr_8a_0_mcgkg,
43
44 m_weight_kg
45) {
46
47 ## Calculate MAP from SBP and DBP: MAP = (2 * DBP + SBP) / 3
48 map <- (2 * daily_dbp_8a_0 + daily_sbp_8a_0) / 3
49
50 ## Calculate norepinephrine equivalents (for vasopressors only)
51 norepi_equiv <- calc_norepi_equivalents(
52 daily_ne_dose_8a_0_mcg = daily_ne_dose_8a_0_mcg,
53 daily_ne_dose_8a_0_mcgkg = daily_ne_dose_8a_0_mcgkg,
54 daily_epi_dose_8a_0_mcg = daily_epi_dose_8a_0_mcg,
55 daily_epi_dose_8a_0_mcgkg = daily_epi_dose_8a_0_mcgkg,
56 daily_phen_dose_8a_0_mcg = daily_phen_dose_8a_0_mcg,
57 daily_phen_dos_8a_0_mcgkg = daily_phen_dos_8a_0_mcgkg,
58 daily_vaso_dose_8a_0 = daily_vaso_dose_8a_0,
59 daily_dopa_dose_8a_0_mcg = daily_dopa_dose_8a_0_mcg,
60 daily_dopa_dos_8a_0_mcgkg = daily_dopa_dos_8a_0_mcgkg,
61 daily_ang2_8a_0_mcg = daily_ang2_8a_0_mcg,
62 daily_ang2_8a_0_mcgkg = daily_ang2_8a_0_mcgkg,
63 m_weight_kg = m_weight_kg
64 )
65
66 ## Calculate dopamine dose in mcg/min/kg for threshold check
67 dopa_dose_mcgkg <- dplyr::coalesce(daily_dopa_dos_8a_0_mcgkg, daily_dopa_dose_8a_0_mcg / m_weight_kg, 0)
68
69 ## Calculate dobutamine and milrinone doses
70 dobuta_dose <- dplyr::coalesce(daily_dobuta_8a_0_mcg, daily_dobuta_8a_0_mcgkg * m_weight_kg, 0)
71 milr_dose <- dplyr::coalesce(daily_milr_8a_0_mcg, daily_milr_8a_0_mcgkg * m_weight_kg, 0)
72
73 ## Check if on any vasopressors (NE, epi, phenylephrine, vasopressin, angiotensin II)
74 on_vasopressors <- is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___1) | # norepinephrine
75 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___2) | # epinephrine
76 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___3) | # phenylephrine
77 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___4) | # vasopressin
78 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___5) | # dopamine
79 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___6) | # dobutamine
80 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___7) | # angiotensin II
81 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___8) | # milrinone
82 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___88) # Other
83
84 ## Check if on OTHER vasopressors (excludes dopamine, dobutamine, milrinone)
85 on_other_vasopressors <- is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___1) | # norepinephrine
86 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___2) | # epinephrine
87 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___3) | # phenylephrine
88 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___4) | # vasopressin
89 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___7) | # angiotensin II
90 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___88) # Other
91
92 dplyr::case_when(
93 # Score 0: No pressors/inotropes, MAP ≥ 70
94 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___0) & (map >= 70) ~ 0,
95
96 # Score 1: No pressors/inotropes, MAP < 70
97 is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___0) & (map < 70) ~ 1,
98
99 # Score 2: (dobutamine/milrinone) AND (no or <= 5 dopamine) AND (no other vasopressors)
100 (is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___6) | is_checked(daily_vasopressors_0___8)) &
101 (dopa_dose_mcgkg <= 5) & !on_other_vasopressors ~ 2,
102
103 # Score 3: On vasopressors with NEE ≤ 0.1
104 on_vasopressors & (norepi_equiv <= 0.1) ~ 3,
105
106 # Score 4: NEE > 0.1
107 norepi_equiv > 0.1 ~ 4,
108 )
109}

Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
crp_0ferritin_0fibrinogen_0ddimer_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_inflamprofile_0(data)
Key assumptions

Four separate three-level biomarker variables using the nearest value from Day 0 back to Day -2, where 0 means not checked rather than low.

  • Inputs are 8 am CRP, ferritin, fibrinogen and D-dimer with their not collected flags from the Daily In-Hospital Forms event.
  • The first non-missing value among Day 0, Day -1 and Day -2 is used.
  • Cutoffs are CRP 15 mg/L, ferritin 700 ng/mL, fibrinogen 150 mg/dL and D-dimer 1500 ng/mL, with 2 for at or above and 1 for below.
  • The value 0 is assigned only when no value exists on any of the three days and at least one day is flagged Not Collected.
  • No value and no Not Collected flag returns NA, and no unit conversion is performed.
  • The output is four columns, crp_0, ferritin_0, fibrinogen_0 and ddimer_0, with no combined score.
Possible issues to confirm
  • For fibrinogen, level 2 is normal or high fibrinogen and level 1 is low, so higher codes do not mean more abnormal.
  • Because 0 means not checked, the codes are not ordinal and should be treated as categorical.
  • The comment on each below-cutoff rule repeats the at-or-above wording.

Output columns
sys_nmblockade_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_nmblockade_0(data)
Key assumptions

Coded 1 only if a paralytic was Administered on Day 0, and any other recorded value, including unknown, is coded 0.

  • Inputs are daily_paralysis_0 and trx_0 from the Daily In-Hospital Forms event, Day 0 only.
  • The value 1 is assigned when daily_paralysis_0 is Administered.
  • The value 0 is assigned when trx_0 is Available and daily_paralysis_0 has any non-missing value other than Administered.
  • The value 0 is also assigned when trx_0 is Not Available and daily_paralysis_0 is missing, so unavailable treatment data are treated as no blockade.
  • Missing daily_paralysis_0 with trx_0 Available returns NA, and there is no unknown code.
Possible issues to confirm
  • A daily_paralysis_0 value such as UNK is coded 0 rather than unknown.

Values:
- 0 = No
- 1 = Yes

Key assumptions

Obstructive lung disease is coded 1 when m_pulmonary is Yes and asthma or COPD is checked.

  • Inputs are m_pulmonary and pulmonary conditions 1 and 3 from the Day 0 event.
  • The value 1 rule is evaluated first and requires m_pulmonary equal to Yes.
  • The value 0 requires m_pulmonary Yes or No with both boxes unchecked.
  • The value 99 is assigned when m_pulmonary is Unknown.
  • A missing m_pulmonary, or No with a box checked, returns NA.

R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_organ_failure_trajectory.R · 375 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sofa_total_day_0sofa_total_day_m1
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_organ_failure_trajectory(data)
Key assumptions

Returns original SOFA totals for Day 0 and Day -1 as separate columns, with every missing or uncomputable component scored 0.

  • Inputs come from the Daily In-Hospital Forms event for Day 0 and Day -1, with weight from the Day 0 event, and no trajectory or difference is computed.
  • Components are summed with na.rm TRUE, so a day with no data totals 0.
  • Day -1 is 99 when dailysofa_perf_m1 is Not Available and NA when dailysofa_perf_m1 is missing, while Day 0 has no such check.
  • Respiratory SOFA uses the worse of P/F and S/F at the lowest PaO2 and SpO2, with S/F invalid above SpO2 97 and standard oxygen FiO2 as 0.21 plus 0.03 times L/min capped at 1.
  • Platelets, bilirubin and creatinine flagged Not Collected score 0, and cardiovascular uses MAP plus dopamine, dobutamine, epinephrine and norepinephrine with missing results set to 0.
  • GCS values containing T or not documented are set to 15 for that day only, with no lookback.
Possible issues to confirm
  • calc_sofa_cns in support_functions.R adds 4 to every GCS, so GCS 15 becomes 19 and scores NA then 0, and GCS 11 scores 0, which understates CNS SOFA.
  • If the not collected fields are NA when a lab value is present, the if_else wrappers return NA and those components are always scored 0.
  • ECMO without invasive ventilation yields NA ratios and therefore 0 respiratory points.
  • Vasopressin and phenylephrine are not considered in the cardiovascular component.
  • The file name lacks the _0 suffix used by the other files, and the Day 0 function parameter name daily_dopa_dose_8a_0_mcgkg differs from the data field daily_dopa_dos_8a_0_mcgkg, though the call is positional.

5# HELPER FUNCTION: Calculate total SOFA score for any day
6# - 6 systems components of SOFA score, each 0-4.
7# - Total SOFA score is sum of 6 sub scores (0-24)
8calc_sofa_total_helper <- function(
9 daily_pa02_lowest,
10 daily_resp_lowest_pao2,
11 daily_fio2_lowest_pao2,
12 daily_o2_lowest_pao2,
13 daily_spo2_lowest,
14 daily_resp_lowest,
15 daily_fio2_lowest,
16 daily_o2_lowest,
17 daily_platelet_8a,
18 daily_platelet_nc,
19 daily_tbili_8a,
20 daily_tbili_nc,
21 daily_sbp_8a,
22 daily_dbp_8a,
23 daily_dopa_dose_8a_mcg,
24 daily_dopa_dos_8a_mcgkg,
25 daily_dobuta_8a_mcg,
26 daily_dobuta_8a_mcgkg,
27 daily_epi_dose_8a_mcg,
28 daily_epi_dose_8a_mcgkg,
29 daily_ne_dose_8a_mcg,
30 daily_ne_dose_8a_mcgkg,
31 m_weight_kg,
32 daily_gcs_8a,
33 daily_cr_8a,
34 daily_cr_nc
35) {
36
37 ## Calculate P/F and S/F ratios for respiratory component
38 pf_ratio <- calc_pf_ratio(
39 low_pao2 = daily_pa02_lowest,
40 resp_low_pao2 = daily_resp_lowest_pao2,
41 fio2_low_pao2 = daily_fio2_lowest_pao2,
42 o2_low_pao2 = daily_o2_lowest_pao2
43 )
44
45 sf_ratio <- calc_sf_ratio(
46 low_spo2 = daily_spo2_lowest,
47 resp_low_spo2 = daily_resp_lowest,
48 fio2_low_spo2 = daily_fio2_lowest,
49 o2_low_spo2 = daily_o2_lowest
50 )
51
52 ## Calculate individual SOFA component scores
53 sofa_resp <- calc_sofa_resp(pf_ratio = pf_ratio, sf_ratio = sf_ratio)
54 sofa_coag <- wrapper_calc_sofa_coag(platelets = daily_platelet_8a, daily_platelet_nc = daily_platelet_nc)
55 sofa_livr <- wrapper_calc_sofa_livr(bilirubin = daily_tbili_8a, daily_tbili_nc = daily_tbili_nc)
56 sofa_card <- wrapper_calc_sofa_card(
57 sbp = daily_sbp_8a,
58 dbp = daily_dbp_8a,
59 dopa_mcg = daily_dopa_dose_8a_mcg,
60 dopa_mcgkg = daily_dopa_dos_8a_mcgkg,
61 dobu_mcg = daily_dobuta_8a_mcg,
62 dobu_mcgkg = daily_dobuta_8a_mcgkg,
63 epin_mcg = daily_epi_dose_8a_mcg,
64 epin_mcgkg = daily_epi_dose_8a_mcgkg,
65 nore_mcg = daily_ne_dose_8a_mcg,
66 nore_mcgkg = daily_ne_dose_8a_mcgkg,
67 weight_kg = m_weight_kg
68 )
69 sofa_cns <- wrapper_calc_sofa_cns(daily_gcs_8a = daily_gcs_8a)
70 sofa_rena <- wrapper_calc_sofa_rena(cr = daily_cr_8a, daily_cr_nc = daily_cr_nc)
71
72 ## Sum all components to get total SOFA score, treating NA as 0
73 total_sofa <- rowSums(
74 cbind(sofa_resp, sofa_coag, sofa_livr, sofa_card, sofa_cns, sofa_rena),
75 na.rm = TRUE
76 )
77
78 return(total_sofa)
79}

297## =============================================================================
298## Wrapper Functions for SOFA Component Scores
299##
300## Currently, the SOFA functions in `support_functions.R` return NA if the SOFA
301## component cannot be calculated (e.g., due to missing data). However, for this
302## DAG variable, we want to treat missing data as 0 points (i.e., normal SOFA
303## score). The wrapper functions below implement that change while preserving the
304## core calculation logic to remain consistent with the original SOFA results.
305##
306## =============================================================================
307
308## Wrapper for calc_sofa_coag that checks for 'Not Collected' status
309## If daily_platelet_nc == 'Not Collected', returns 0 points
310## Otherwise calls calc_sofa_coag with the platelet value
311wrapper_calc_sofa_coag <- function(platelets, daily_platelet_nc) {
312 dplyr::if_else(
313 daily_platelet_nc == 'Not Collected',
314 0,
315 calc_sofa_coag(platelets = platelets)
316 )
317}
318

321## If daily_tbili_nc == 'Not Collected', returns 0 points

325 daily_tbili_nc == 'Not Collected',

327 calc_sofa_livr(bilirubin = bilirubin)
328 )
329}

Presence of ARDS Syndrome

R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_ards_0.R · 113 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sys_ards_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_ards_0(data, dictionary)
Key assumptions

ARDS requires bilateral opacities on Day -2 to Day 0 plus Day 0 hypoxemia on IMV, NIV, HFNC or ECMO with IMV, and missing oxygenation data yields 0, not NA.

  • Bilateral opacity uses d0_pos, dm1_pos and dm2_pos from the Syndrome Adjudication event, and any one equal to 1 satisfies the criterion.
  • SpO2 option requires lowest Day 0 SpO2 at most 97 and SpO2 divided by FiO2 at most 315 with respiratory support code 1, 3, 4 or 5.
  • PaO2 option requires lowest Day 0 PaO2 divided by FiO2 at that time at most 300 with respiratory support code 1, 3, 4 or 5.
  • Oxygenation is taken from Day 0 only, with no lookback, and FiO2 is assumed to be recorded as a fraction.
  • Because each oxygenation option is FALSE when any input is missing, a patient with no usable Day 0 oxygenation data is coded 0.
  • NA is returned only when the opacity criterion is NA and the oxygenation criterion is met.
  • Standard oxygen, room air and ECMO without IMV do not qualify, and no PEEP threshold is applied.
Possible issues to confirm
  • The header says NA means insufficient data, but missing oxygenation inputs are silently coded 0.
  • A patient with opacity fields partly 0 and partly NA and failing oxygenation is coded 0 rather than unknown.

2## Presence of ARDS Syndrome (Systematic & Streamlined DAG)
3## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
4
5# Calculate SYSTEMATIC DAG 'Presence of ARDS Syndrome'
6#
7# Values:
8# - 0 = Syndrome criteria not all present
9# - 1 = Syndrome criteria all present
10# - NA = Unknown/insufficient data
11calc_sys_ards_0 <- function(
12 d0_pos,
13 dm1_pos,
14 dm2_pos,
15 daily_spo2_lowest_0,
16 daily_fio2_lowest_0,
17 daily_resp_lowest_0_code,
18 daily_pa02_lowest_0,
19 daily_fio2_lowest_pao2_0,
20 daily_resp_lowest_pao2_0_code
21) {
22
23 ## Criterion #1: Bilateral opacities on or before Day 0
24 criterion_1 <- (d0_pos == 1 | dm1_pos == 1 | dm2_pos == 1)
25
26 ## Criterion #2 Option A: SpO2-based hypoxemia with qualifying respiratory support
27 # Qualifying respiratory support codes: 1=ECMO+IMV, 3=IMV, 4=NIV, 5=HFNC
28 option_a <- (
29 !is.na(daily_spo2_lowest_0) &
30 !is.na(daily_fio2_lowest_0) &
31 !is.na(daily_resp_lowest_0_code) &
32 daily_spo2_lowest_0 <= 97 &
33 (daily_spo2_lowest_0 / daily_fio2_lowest_0) <= 315 &
34 daily_resp_lowest_0_code %in% c(1, 3, 4, 5)
35 )
36
37 ## Criterion #2 Option B: PaO2-based hypoxemia with qualifying respiratory support
38 option_b <- (
39 !is.na(daily_pa02_lowest_0) &
40 !is.na(daily_fio2_lowest_pao2_0) &
41 !is.na(daily_resp_lowest_pao2_0_code) &
42 (daily_pa02_lowest_0 / daily_fio2_lowest_pao2_0) <= 300 &
43 daily_resp_lowest_pao2_0_code %in% c(1, 3, 4, 5)
44 )
45
46 ## Criterion #2: Either Option A or Option B is met
47 criterion_2 <- (option_a | option_b)
48
49 ## Determine ARDS status
50 dplyr::case_when(
51 # Both criteria met -> ARDS present
52 criterion_1 & criterion_2 ~ 1,
53 # Either criterion definitively not met -> ARDS not present
54 (!is.na(criterion_1) & !criterion_1) | (!is.na(criterion_2) & !criterion_2) ~ 0,
55 # Otherwise -> Unknown
56 TRUE ~ NA_real_
57 )
58}

80 left_join(
81 get_code_label_map('daily_resp_lowest_0', dictionary),

83 ) |>
84 left_join(
85 get_code_label_map('daily_resp_lowest_pao2_0', dictionary),

87 ) |>

96 ),

111 )) |>
112 select(record_id, sys_ards_0)
113}

Presence of Pneumonia Syndrome

R/steroid-dag-variables/calc_sys_pneumonia_0.R · 377 lines
Latest on mainPermalink 6ea8edbEdit fileHistory
Output columns
sys_pneumonia_0
Call
wrapper_calc_sys_pneumonia_0(data, dictionary)
Key assumptions

Requires opacity, a fever or WBC or elderly altered mental status sign, symptoms, and antimicrobial or pathogen evidence, and most incomplete records resolve to 0, not NA.

  • Opacity uses d0_pos, dm1_pos or dm2_pos equal to 1, or any CXR or CT opacity code 1 on Day -2 to Day 0, from the Syndrome Adjudication event.
  • The sign criterion is Day 0 highest temperature above 38 C, WBC at least 12 or at most 4 on Day -2 to Day 0, or age 70 plus with GCS below 15 off IMV.
  • GCS values with T or not documented are set to 15, so intubated or undocumented patients cannot meet altered mental status.
  • Symptoms use pna_cdc3 Yes, or, only when pna_cdc3 is missing, at least 2 of 4 symptom groups from pna_symptoms boxes 1 or 2, 4 to 6, 7, and 8.
  • Antimicrobial evidence is Day 0 antibiotics Administered, Day 0 antiviral Administered with antiviral type 2, 6 to 13 or 15, or pathogen codes 1 to 5, 7, 8 or 17 to 21 by enrollment.
  • Missing temperature, WBC or GCS are treated as criterion not met, so such patients are coded 0.
  • After the main rules, pna_cdc3 No, or any recorded antibiotic or antiviral value including Administered and UNK, forces 0.
Possible issues to confirm
  • The fallback rules code 0 even when daily_antibiotics_0 is Administered, so a patient with unknown opacity status is coded 0 instead of NA.
  • The header says NA means unknown, but because the sign criterion is never NA, nearly all incomplete records are coded 0.
  • Highest temperature is not swapped with lowest temperature, although the APS file notes the high value can be lower than the low value.
  • COVID-19 code 6 and influenza codes 15 and 16 are excluded from the qualifying pathogen list.

- 0 = PNU1 syndrome criteria + antimicrobial criterion not all present
- 1 = PNU1 syndrome criteria + antimicrobial criterion all present
